sources.name: MoEYS scholarships page (ក្រសួងអប់រំ យុវជន និងកីឡា – អាហារូបករណ៍)
sources.what: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport listing of government-to-government scholarship announcements (Hungary, China, Korea, Japan, Russia, Azerbaijan, Turkey, etc.) as PDF/Khmer notices; the Department of Scholarships under the Directorate General of Higher Education publishes here. Site is slow and often unindexed; the Facebook page carries the same notices faster.

sources.name: MoEYS Cambodia Facebook page
sources.what: Official ministry page (~4.2M likes). Posts every scholarship announcement as image/PDF of the Khmer សេចក្តីជូនដំណឹង letter: ASEAN Scholarship, Stipendium Hungaricum, China-ASEAN Digital Academy, MEXT, GKS, Russian and Azerbaijani offers, and the domestic 100%-tuition bachelor scholarships (10,554 places for 2026-27). This is the single most-followed source for G2G scholarships.

sources.name: MoEYS News Telegram (ព័ត៌មានអប់រំ យុវជន និងកីឡា)
sources.what: Official MoEYS Telegram channel that mirrors ministry notices including scholarship announcements.

sources.name: ប្រព័ន្ធអាហារូបករណ៍ឧត្តមសិក្សា – DGHE higher-education scholarship system
sources.what: Directorate General of Higher Education online portal for the domestic MoEYS scholarships (bachelor/master/PhD places at public HEIs) that students apply to after Bac II results.

sources.name: Australia Awards Cambodia – Scholarships
sources.what: Official DFAT-managed programme site: intake brochure, eligibility (IELTS 6.0 for master's coursework), priority fields, OASIS application link. 2027 intake opened 1 Feb 2026 and closed 30 Apr 2026 at 14:00 AEST.

sources.name: EducationUSA Advising Center – U.S. Embassy in Cambodia
sources.what: Free advising on U.S. study and scholarships. Centers at Exchange Square Mall Phnom Penh (Floor 1, No. 19-20 St 106, +855 10 502 121, PhnomPenh@educationusa.org) and Siem Reap; Opportunity Funds programme for high-achieving low-income students; annual EducationUSA Fair each October.

sources.name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program – U.S. Embassy in Cambodia
sources.what: Annual call for Cambodian master's/PhD candidates. 2027-28 cycle: application at apply.iie.org/ffsp2027, deadline 30 April 2026 23:59 ET, later extended to 5 June 2026. IELTS 7.0 typical.

sources.name: Embassy of Japan in Cambodia – Scholarship section
sources.what: Index of MEXT (Japanese Government) scholarship pages: general info, Research, Undergraduate, KOSEN, Specialized Training College, Teacher Training, past exam papers. Scholarship Advisor: scholarship.jpn@pp.mofa.go.jp, Tel 023-217-161~4, office hours 13:30-17:15.

sources.name: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Cambodia – Announcements
sources.what: Announcement board where GKS Embassy Track calls are posted: GKS-U (undergraduate) each Sept (2026 cycle 15-30 Sept 2025, offline submission required, 3 Cambodia slots), GKS-G (graduate) each Feb (2026 cycle 12-25 Feb, 12 Cambodia slots), AKS Korean Studies track, TOPIK schedule at CKCC.

sources.name: Study in Korea – GKS notices and online application
sources.what: NIIED portal where GKS guidelines and the university list are published and where GKS-U online applications are submitted.

sources.name: Embassy of the People's Republic of China in Cambodia
sources.what: Official embassy site; Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC Type A, embassy channel) notices for the 2026/27 year required online application at campuschina.org plus documents to the embassy by mid-February 2026 (8-14 Feb). Contact chinaemb_kh@mfa.gov.cn. Cambodia gets roughly 30-50 embassy-channel slots plus ASEAN and China-ASEAN Digital Academy places announced via MoEYS.

sources.name: Campus China – CSC online application
sources.what: China Scholarship Council portal where all Chinese Government Scholarship applications (Type A embassy and Type B university) are created; window normally December to April.

sources.name: Campus France Cambodge – Obtenir une bourse
sources.what: Official French study office in Phnom Penh: France Excellence (ex-BGF) master's/PhD scholarships managed by the French Embassy, Eiffel programme, Campus Bourses search. 2025-26 campaign opened 16 Dec 2024 with deadline 26 Jan 2025 18:00; applications to campusfrance@ifcambodge.com.

sources.name: DAAD in Cambodia (DAAD Regional Office Hanoi)
sources.what: DAAD has no office in Phnom Penh; the Hanoi regional office covers Cambodia, and a DAAD long-term lecturer at RUPP's Department of Media and Communication is the on-the-ground contact for DAAD scholarship questions (EPOS, research grants).

sources.name: Chevening – Cambodia
sources.what: Official Chevening country page. 2027-28 cycle opened 4 Aug 2026, closes 6 Oct 2026 11:00 UTC; requires 2 years (2,400 hours) work experience; British Embassy Phnom Penh shortlists and interviews; unconditional UK offer due 8 July 2027.

sources.name: EU Delegation to Cambodia – Travel & Study (Erasmus+)
sources.what: EU Delegation page on Erasmus+ / Erasmus Mundus opportunities for Cambodians; the Delegation runs the annual European Scholarship Fair in Phnom Penh with 'Team Europe' embassies and info sessions at provincial universities.

sources.name: Stipendium Hungaricum – Cambodia
sources.what: Hungarian government programme page for Cambodia; MoEYS is the sending partner that publishes the local call and nominates. Application at apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu, deadline 15 January (14:00 CET); nominations by end of February.

sources.name: ASEAN Scholarships for Cambodia – Singapore MOE
sources.what: Singapore Ministry of Education secondary/pre-university scholarship (Secondary 3 to Pre-U 2, GCE A-Level). Cambodian applications open around 1 April and close end of May (2023: 5 Apr-31 May); selection test and interview in Phnom Penh; MoEYS Facebook also posts the call.

sources.name: UWC Cambodia national committee
sources.what: Selects Cambodian students in grades 11-12 for UWC two-year IB scholarships. Application deadline 15 November 2026; multi-stage selection (tests, group tasks, interview). Contact selection@kh.uwc.org or fb.me/uwc.cambodia.

sources.name: New Zealand Scholarships – Cambodia Facebook
sources.what: Page used for Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship calls in Cambodia.

sources.name: RUPP scholarship announcements
sources.what: Running list of scholarship and exchange announcements posted by RUPP.

sources.name: Cambodia Academy of Digital Technology (CADT) Telegram
sources.what: Official CADT channel; posts digital-technology scholarships (e.g. the 500+ MoEYS digital scholarships, China-ASEAN Digital Academy).

sources.name: Scholarship for Cambodia (Facebook)
sources.what: Largest community scholarship page (~167K followers); reposts embassy, MoEYS, university and NGO scholarships with Khmer summaries and links.

sources.name: WEduShare
sources.what: Cambodia's largest online opportunity platform (founded 2016; ~233K Facebook fans, 10K newsletter subscribers): scholarship listings with deadlines, how-to articles, Khmer explainers such as 'fully funded scholarships for Cambodian students', plus Facebook, Instagram and Telegram channels.

sources.name: Ahladang – អាឡាដាំង (Facebook)
sources.what: Education page (~147K likes) started 2015; scholarship information, free online mentoring for rural students, English lessons and application tips.

sources.name: Study Abroad Center មជ្ឈមណ្ឌលអាហារូបករណ៍សិក្សាក្រៅប្រទេស
sources.what: Khmer-language page (~146K likes) reposting scholarships with tips; linked to a study-abroad consultancy.

sources.name: Federation of Cambodian Students Abroad – CamStudent (Telegram)
sources.what: Channel (~5K subscribers) of the federation of Cambodian student associations overseas; shares scholarship calls and first-hand advice from students already abroad.
